description:
Redwood Inference will deploy a lightweight, always-on performance canary in production to detect and alert on serving-runtime regressions (primarily p95 latency and tokens/sec) on a per-model basis. The canary is intended to catch tail-latency and throughput regressions caused by kernel changes, scheduling/batching heuristics, model config updates, GPU fleet changes, or rollouts—before broad customer impact.

Goals:
- Detect p95 latency regressions and tokens/sec drops per model (and optionally per region/tier) with low noise.
- Provide fast triage signals that help isolate whether a regression is kernel-level, scheduler-level, model-config-level, or infrastructure-level.
- Integrate with existing observability (dashboards, alerting, incident bot) and rollout workflows (canary/rollback gates).
- Keep canary overhead minimal (target: <0.5% GPU capacity per region for covered models) and avoid collecting customer data.

Scope:
- Canary workload: synthetic prompt distribution representing typical production shapes (prefill/decode mix, prompt length buckets), running against a curated set of “top models” and “high-risk models” (newly onboarded, recently optimized kernels, etc.).
- Metrics: p50/p95/p99 latency (end-to-end and runtime-only), tokens/sec, prefill latency, decode latency, queueing time, batch size distribution, KV cache hit rate (where applicable).
- Baselines: per model + runtime version + hardware SKU (+ optionally region) stored and versioned; regression defined as percentage deviation beyond thresholds with minimum sample size.
- Alerting: tiered alerts (warning vs paging), anti-flap logic, and routing to #eng-runtime and #eng-oncall with clear runbook links.
- Production rollout: start in one region with 2–3 models, tune thresholds for 1–2 weeks, then expand model coverage and regions; add gating integration with release engineering.

Out of scope (initially):
- Customer-traffic shadowing that might capture customer prompts; advanced quality-eval coupling (handled by Applied ML / eval harness separately).

Key stakeholders:
- Serving Runtime (Kernel + Scheduling): Mateo Alvarez (exec sponsor), Hiro Tanaka, Sofia Ivanova, Noah Patel, Omar El-Sayed, Samir Qureshi.
- SRE / On-call: Sean Gallagher, Rafael Mendes, Aisha Bello, Allison Grant.
- Platform Telemetry/Observability: Logan Wright, Nadia Rahman, Caleb Johnson.
- Product (Console & Rollouts): Marissa Cole, Paula Mendes.

Proposed timeline (8–10 weeks):
1) Requirements & design (Week 1–2): metric definitions, baseline strategy, model coverage list, privacy constraints.
2) Implementation (Week 3–5): perf-canary service + runtime instrumentation + telemetry pipeline.
3) Dashboards/alerts/runbooks (Week 4–6): SLO toolkit wiring, alert policies, incident bot routing.
4) Controlled rollout (Week 6–8): single region, limited models; threshold tuning and false-positive reduction.
5) Expansion + rollout gates (Week 8–10): broader coverage, optional integration with release freeze / auto-rollback signals.

Deliverables:
- perf-canary service deployment and configuration (Helm/terraform + runtime integration).
- Baseline and threshold configuration per model.
- Dashboards + alert policies + runbooks.
- Post-launch retro and follow-up backlog (noise reduction, additional models, deeper attribution signals).

files.description: Primary design doc: architecture of the prod perf canary, workload model, metrics captured, baseline strategy, attribution signals (kernel vs scheduler), and rollout plan.
ADR documenting baseline computation (rolling vs fixed), regression thresholds, minimum sample sizes, and anti-flap logic tradeoffs.
Dashboard spec: per-model p95 latency/tokens-sec panels, breakdown by prefill/decode/queueing, and links to traces/logs.
Defines how per-model performance alerts map to SLO concepts (warning vs page), notification routing, and ownership expectations.
On-call runbook: how to validate alerts, compare to baseline, identify likely cause (runtime release, kernel change, fleet change), mitigation/rollback steps, and escalation paths.
Operational runbook for deploying/upgrading the canary service across regions, including rollback and safe-disable procedures.
Performance/safety standards: GPU overhead budgets, QPS limits, isolation requirements, and data-handling rules (no customer prompts).
Reference doc for the synthetic prompt distribution used by the canary (length buckets, prefill/decode mix) and rationale.
Postmortem after early rollout: root cause of false positives (baseline drift/cardinality), remediation (thresholds, smoothing), and follow-ups.
Validation plan: staging bake, replay tests, noise characterization, and acceptance criteria before enabling paging in prod.
Working kickoff notes: open questions, initial model coverage list, owners, and links to early dashboards/queries.
Spreadsheet-style doc: per-model baseline stats, proposed regression thresholds, sample size requirements, and tuning notes by region/SKU.
Initial baseline results from staging/prod shadow environment; includes tables for latency/tokens-sec distributions and variance observations.
Working memo assessing metric label cardinality risks, proposed label set, and cost/retention impact.
Draft alerting policies and routing; includes 'page vs warn' decision notes, dampening strategy, and escalation matrix.
Scratchpad describing the synthetic prompts (shape only), generation parameters, and rationale for representing production workloads without customer data.
Release checklist used by eng-releases: enabling canary per region, verifying dashboards, and confirming rollback automation hooks.
Retro notes after initial rollout: what worked, what was noisy, action items for next iteration.
Umbrella engineering ticket for MVP canary: scope, milestones, sub-issues, and acceptance criteria.
Defines exact metric names/labels, required dimensions (model, version, region), and expected query patterns for alerting.
Implements baseline storage strategy (per model/version/SKU) and update policy; includes discussion of drift and seasonality.
Adds/validates scheduler-level instrumentation to attribute regressions to queueing vs execution time.
Adds kernel selection/version tags so regressions can be correlated to kernel rollouts or auto-selection changes.
Tracks dashboard creation work (observability-pack) and required panels for runtime/SRE triage.
Alert rules, paging thresholds, and incident-bot integration; includes noise budget and anti-flap requirements.
Deployment work: Helm chart wiring, environment config, and rollout sequencing across regions.
Rollout ticket for first region + small model set; includes monitoring checklist and sign-off from SRE/runtime.
Follow-up ticket to add additional models after tuning; includes capacity/overhead validation.
PM ticket: integrate canary signals into rollout decision-making (pause/rollback criteria, UX/notifications).
Backlog item: reduce false positives via smoothing, baseline drift handling, and region/SKU-aware thresholds.
Creates the on-call runbook and defines escalation paths between runtime, infra, and telemetry teams.
Adds a lightweight CI check to ensure canary metrics are emitted correctly and dashboards/alerts don’t break on deploy.
Initial PR creating the perf-canary service skeleton, config layout, and basic request loop against internal inference endpoints.
Adds prompt-shape generator (length buckets, parameters) and a seedable workload profile to keep runs reproducible.
Adds metric emission for end-to-end latency and tokens/sec with per-model labels and guardrails on cardinality.
Implements baseline lookup and regression evaluation logic (min samples, rolling window, percent-change thresholds).
Adds config to run canary per region and hardware SKU; includes safeguards to prevent accidental wide fanout.
Implements QPS caps and a capacity budget to keep the canary below target GPU overhead.
Adds explicit assertions and logging redaction to ensure no customer prompts or identifiers are stored/emitted.
Adds standardized alert payload formatting (model, baseline, observed, confidence, links) for incident-bot ingestion.
Exports scheduler queueing-time metrics and batch-size distribution needed for canary attribution.
Adds runtime build tags and kernel-selection identifiers to telemetry so regressions correlate with releases/kernels.
Introduces a restricted auth scope/service account for perf-canary to call inference endpoints safely.
Adds control-plane config surface to define canary model list per region/tier with validation and audit logging.
Adds shared aggregation helper for per-model metrics normalization (units, histograms) used by canary and dashboards.
Adds Grafana dashboard panels for per-model p95 latency, tokens/sec, and breakdowns; includes links to runbooks.
Adds warning-level alert rules with dampening and minimum sample size conditions; routes to #eng-runtime.
Adds paging rules (Sev2/Sev1) for sustained regressions on top models; routes to on-call rotation channel.
Introduces SLO templates for per-model performance signals and guidance for selecting thresholds.
Adds a job to compute baseline distributions from a controlled load run; outputs baseline artifacts consumed by perf-canary.
Adds Helm chart for perf-canary with safe defaults, resource requests, and environment/region configuration.
Terraform changes: service account, secret management, and least-privilege IAM bindings for canary deployment.
